recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-13231 in the core FHIR source unless a future work-group decision reopens the Timing datatype semantics.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive MnM change request for STU3 asking to change the Timing datatype introduction so Timing can describe expected or requested occurrences and summaries of past or ongoing events, while noting that future-tense component definitions can also describe historic or ongoing events.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied in git-svn commit 993e3553281c688e717a529b060d1b10e226f011, whose message references #13231 and svn revision 12466. That commit changed source/datatypes.html from the earlier shorter Timing introduction to the requested two-paragraph wording and updated source/datatypes/timing.xml with the same text.
additional_context: Timing remains an active current datatype in source/fhir.ini and is marked normative. The earlier same-family FHIR-12637 removed the explicit statement that Timing was not used for past events, and the related Zulip discussion shows why broader wording across future, current, and past timing information was needed. No directly relevant later Zulip or Confluence record was found that contradicts the current source state.
reconciliation: No source change was made because source/datatypes.html already says Timing may represent summaries of past or ongoing events and clarifies that future-tense component definitions can describe historic or ongoing events.
